quiz.title: Quiz 3 - Ratio and Proportion
quiz.instructions: Choose one answer for each question. Work out your answer before checking, then use the worked solution to review your method. Give exact answers unless stated otherwise. A calculator may be used.

questions.title: Question 1
questions.working:
The highest common factor of 42 and 70 is 14. Divide both parts by 14:

\(42:70=3:5\).

questions.title: Question 2
questions.prompt: Amira and Ben share €156 in the ratio \(5:7\). How much does Ben receive?
questions.working:
There are \(5+7=12\) parts. One part is \(156\div12=13\) euros. Ben receives 7 parts:

\(7\times13=91\) euros.

\(150:60=5:2\) after dividing by 30.

questions.title: Question 4
questions.prompt: Seven identical notebooks cost €12.60. The cost is directly proportional to the number bought. How much do 11 notebooks cost?
questions.working: One notebook costs \(12.60\div7=1.80\) euros. Eleven cost \(11\times1.80=19.80\) euros.

questions.title: Question 5
questions.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=5\), \(y=35\). Find \(y\) when \(x=8\).

questions.title: Question 6
questions.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x^2\). When \(x=4\), \(y=48\). Find \(y\) when \(x=6\).

questions.title: Question 7
questions.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\), with \(x>0\). When \(x=6\), \(y=8\). Find \(y\) when \(x=4\).

questions.title: Question 8
questions.prompt: Six workers take 15 days to complete a job. Assume all workers have the same constant rate and the time is inversely proportional to the number of workers. How long would ten workers take?
questions.working: The job needs \(6\times15=90\) worker-days. With ten workers the time is \(\frac{90}{10}=9\) days.

questions.section: Developing - Inverse squares and square roots
questions.title: Question 9
questions.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x^2\), where \(x>0\). When \(x=2\), \(y=45\). Find \(y\) when \(x=6\).

questions.section: Developing - Inverse squares and square roots
questions.title: Question 10
questions.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{x}\), where \(x>0\). When \(x=25\), \(y=10\). Find \(y\) when \(x=100\).

questions.section: Developing - Inverse squares and square roots
questions.title: Question 11
questions.prompt: \(z\) is inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{w}\), where \(w>0\). When \(w=36\), \(z=4\). Express \(z\) in terms of \(w\).

questions.title: Question 12
questions.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x^2\), with \(x>0\) and \(y>0\). If \(x\) is multiplied by 3, what happens to \(y\)?

questions.title: Question 13
questions.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{x}\), with \(x>0\) and \(y>0\). If \(x\) is divided by 9, what happens to \(y\)?
questions.working: Since \(\sqrt{\frac{x}{9}}=\frac{\sqrt{x}}{3}\), the denominator becomes one third as large. Thus \(\frac{k}{\sqrt{x}/3}=3\frac{k}{\sqrt{x}}=3y\).

questions.title: Question 14
questions.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x^2\), where \(x>0\). When \(x=3\), \(y=32\). Find \(x\) when \(y=18\).

questions.title: Question 15
questions.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{x}\), with \(x>0\) and \(y>0\). The value of \(y\) decreases by 20%. By what factor is \(x\) multiplied?
questions.working:
A 20% decrease gives \(y_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{4}{5}y_{\mathrm{old}}\). Since \(y=\frac{k}{\sqrt{x}}\), the square root of \(x\) must be multiplied by \(\frac{5}{4}\). Squaring this factor gives

\(\frac{x_{\mathrm{new}}}{x_{\mathrm{old}}}=\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2=\frac{25}{16}\).
